title: tests/allocations.rs counts other threads, so the admission test fails about 2% of runs
body:
`resource_admission_allocates_nothing_when_ready_or_waiting` sometimes sees allocations it didn't make. The counting allocator sums every thread's bytes, and the test harness's own threads allocate while the call runs. The file and `src/admission.rs` are unchanged from next fbfb319f.

- Ice mutation gate on 88e215ed (`r88-quality-ice-20261108T164307-8962d124`, FAILED, retained): one shard's **unmutated baseline** failed with `left: 900`, and the gate stopped there with no verdict.
- ARM VM, 88e215ed, 400 processes 16 at a time (`r88-alloc-diag-arm-20261108T164802-b14bddbd`): the original test failed **7 of 400** (892 B). A diagnostic counting other threads apart: 396 runs 0 bytes, 4 runs 796–892 bytes, **every byte from another thread**.
- Test-only fix 3d26a42e on personal `test/sam-r88-x86-quality` gives each thread its own count (a const thread-local; the calls measured are single-threaded): **0 of 400** failures (`r88-alloc-fixed-arm-20261108T165029-772fab44`).

The same branch's next commit, 10454b8a, adds the six GPU-only `take_run` rows to the x86 registry, as for ddb7199d. Its Ice gate is queued; I will post the verdict on #303.

— Sam Shackleton
